preamble: Insertion of [k] occurs as an excrescent stop between the velar nasal [ŋ] and a following voiceless fricative or sibilant: the velar closure is held while the velum rises for the fricative, producing a brief oral [k] release. English length and strength commonly have an optional [k] of this kind, and the Sanskrit grammarian Pāṇini formalized the same optional augment (kuk) after word-final ṅ before a sibilant.

examples.note: Optional excrescent [k] between [ŋ] and the voiceless dental fricative [θ]; dictionaries give /lɛŋ(k)θ/ for British, American and Canadian English.
Same environment and the same optional excrescent [k].
Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.28 (ṅaṇoḥ kukṭuk śari) optionally adds the augment k after word-final ṅ before a sibilant; the parallel rule adds ṭ after ṇ (vaṇ śete ~ vaṇṭ śete).
Same rule before the retroflex sibilant ṣ.

sources: Pāṇini, Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.28, with Kāśikā commentary (2026 online edition). sanskritdocuments.org. https://sanskritdocuments.org/learning_tools/ashtadhyayi/vyakhya/8/8.3.28.htm
